I used to love going out with friends, picking outfits, dancing at shows—now nothing feels fun. I’ll be in the middle of a shoot, and someone laughs, and I just feel… empty. Like I’m watching it through glass. And honestly, I’ve been blaming my ex for a lot of it—he was supposed to pick me up that night, but he didn’t. I know it’s not that simple, but I keep replaying it like he could’ve stopped it.

I’ve been forgetting things too—where I left my phone, client names, even appointments. Not like I’m distracted; it’s like my mind just blanks. And if someone walks into a room too fast, I flinch. Hard. Like my body’s always ready to run.

There’s this thought that loops sometimes: *What if it had been worse?* Over and over. I don’t do anything to stop it—it just won’t stop.
D018-D016_h001.question_a:
I’ve been having these flashes—like, out of nowhere—of that night last year when I was mugged. I see his face, the knife, the alley behind the boutique... it comes back in full detail, and I can’t shut it out. It happens when I’m styling shoots, even during client meetings. I’ll just freeze for a second, heart racing.  

Since then, nothing feels good anymore. I used to love curating looks, finding the perfect piece—now it’s just... empty. My friends say I’ve pulled away; I don’t go out, don’t feel anything, not even when my sister hugs me. I keep thinking, *Why did the store owner just close early that night? I’m always on edge. Someone walks into the room too fast, or a phone drops—I flinch like I’m back there. I forget things too—where I left my keys, appointments—even during fittings. It’s like my brain’s always scanning for danger.  

These thoughts about the attack? They’re constant. But I don’t do any rituals, don’t wash my hands or check things—I just relive it. It’s not random; it’s always tied to *that moment*. It hasn’t faded at all. The horror is still right there, like it just happened.

I keep blaming my friend who was driving that night—if she hadn’t insisted we go out, it never would’ve happened. The fear from that moment just… sticks with me, like I’m still in it.

I’ve been forgetting things too—where I put my keys, client names during meetings—which I think is from being so scattered and tense. I jump whenever someone walks up behind me suddenly; even a quick hand motion across my vision sets me off.

I know it sounds irrational, but I can’t stop. These aren’t about the crash—they’re completely separate, but the urge to do the tapping, to "fix" it, is overwhelming.
